data.name: Gina
data.gender_notes: Gina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Gina is derived from the Greek word 'ginosko' which means 'to know, to be acquainted with, to recognise'. It was also used as a diminutive of the Greek name 'Virginia'. The name Gina carries the meaning “Joy, Pure, Loving” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Gina usually hope their child will grow to embody joy, pure, loving and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Gina is a name that signifies knowledge, understanding, and wisdom. It is a name that embodies the spiritual qualities of being aware, mindful, and intuitive.
data.etymology: Gina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joy, Pure, Loving.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gina total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: גִּינָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: גִּינָה (Ginah) היא שם נשי שמקורו בעברית קדומה, והוא קשור למושגים של פרי, גבורה, אנושות, חזקה ובת. בתי כנסת קדומים משתמשים בשם זה כדי לתאר את חזון הנשים כגבורות וכבעלות כוח. בספר תהלים (31:10), האלוהים יוצר את אשת דוד, שושן לבן, ואומר 'עֹזֶרֶת - אָבִיהָ', כלומר, 'אשת העזרה של אביה', אשר מראה את הסמכות הנשית של חזון הנשים.

in_greek.name: Γίνα
in_greek.long_meaning: Γίνα (Gína) είναι ένα γυναικείο όνομα στην αρχαία ελληνική, που σχετίζεται με τις έννοιες του παιδός, της γυναίκας, της καλότητας και του ωραίου. Στην ελληνική μυθολογία, η Γίνα ήταν η μορφή της ερωτικής αγάπης και της φύσης. Στον Νέο Διατάγμα, η Γίνα δεν είναι ένα επίσημο όνομα, αλλά έχει χρησιμοποιηθεί ως έπαινο για τις γυναίκες, που δisplay την καλή και την ωραία.

in_latin.name: Gina
in_latin.long_meaning: Gina est nomen femininum quod ad feminam, puellam, pulchram, et bonam refert. In historia Ecclesiae, Ginae erant mulieres, quae in virtute et caritate excelluerunt, et exemplo fuerunt viris. In Novo Testamento, nomen Ginae non explicit mentionatur, sed mulieres, qui virtutem et caritatem manifestaverunt, sunt exemplum bonae Ginae.

in_english.name: Gina
in_english.long_meaning: Gina is a feminine given name that originates from the Hebrew name 'Ginah' or the Greek name 'Gina', meaning feminine, girl, good, beautiful, or pleasant. In Christian tradition, the name Gina is associated with virtues such as kindness, compassion, and generosity. In modern times, the name Gina has been popularized by various cultural and social contexts, including the Gina Lollobrigida, a famous Italian actress, and Gina Haspel, the first female Director of the Central Intelligence Agency. As a given name, Gina is often bestowed upon girls born to Christian families, symbolizing the values of femininity, goodness, and beauty.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gina gained popularity in the western world, particularly during the Renaissance period when Greek names experienced a resurgence in usage. The name is feminine and carries a sense of sophistication and elegance. It is also associated with the figure of St. Gianna, a Catholic saint and doctor who is known for her strong faith, selflessness, and devotion to her patients.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Gina holds a deeper spiritual significance as it is connected to the idea of knowledge, understanding, and recognition. It is a reminder that true wisdom and insight come from a deep connection with God and a willingness to learn from His teachings. The name also encourages us to strive for self-awareness and to recognize the unique gifts and talents that we possess as children of God. By embracing the meaning behind the name Gina, we can seek to cultivate a deeper relationship with God and a greater understanding of the world around us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gina: Derived from the Hebrew name "Elena," meaning "shining light." In Christianity, Gina represents the radiant spirit of a woman who illuminates the lives of those around her with her love and compassion.

historical_references.reference: The legend of St. Genevieve, a Parisian virgin-saint, relates that she was born around 422 AD in the village of Nanterre. She lived during the time of the Huns invasion and subsequent siege of Paris around 451 AD.

Another legend tells the story of St. Gina, an Arab Christian woman from the city of Nisibis in Mesopotamia, who lived during the period of the Crusades in the late 11th and early 12th centuries AD. She was renowned for her acts of courage and mercy during the siege of Tripoli by the Crusaders in 1102 AD.
